Subject: Recap + pricing inputs request (FinovateCo proof-of-concept)

Hi Sofia — great chat earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and the inputs we need to size an accurate POC pricing profile for you: 

Call recap (2 pager):
- Goal: 6-week POC to validate Summarization + Assist flows inside your advisor console; measure latency and quality over 10k sessions.
- Primary model constraints: must support long context for multi-document summarization and citation (some cases > 8k tokens).
- Success metric: median end-to-end latency < 800ms for typical flows and cost ≤ budget envelope.

What we need from you to finalize a scoped estimate:
1) Typical token mix: avg prompt tokens per request, avg completion tokens per request (mean and 90th pct).
2) Percent of responses requiring >2k, >8k, >32k, and any >128k contexts (even if rare).
3) Expected daily active sessions and approximate monthly active users (MAU) or monthly request volume.
4) Target budget range for the POC (monthly), and any target unit economics (e.g., target $/1M tokens).

I attached a short CSV template (finovate_volume_profile.csv) you can fill — if easier, paste numbers inline and I’ll incorporate them. I’ll also run a quick cost simulation (attached redwood_cost_sim.xlsx) showing three scenarios (8k-primary, 32k-mixed, 128k-edge) and approximate $ per 1M tokens under different batching & quantization profiles.

Next steps: if you can send the numbers by EOD Monday I’ll turn this into a formal quote and share with Lauren for approved discounting. Also confirm whether procurement needs an SOW or an initial MSA for the POC.

— Ben

Thanks Sofia — super helpful. I pulled together an initial unit-econ sketch and a few sensitivity scenarios; attaching the workbook (redwood_cost_sim.xlsx) and pasted the headline calculations below so you have them immediately.

Headline unit economics (blended scenarios):
- Inputs from you: 108M prompt tokens / month, 405M completion tokens / month => ~513M tokens/month.
- Baseline hosted estimate (8k-optimized model for majority flows): approximate cost range $9–$25 per 1M tokens depending on batching & quantization.
- Mix-adjusted blended target: with 1% of requests requiring >8k contexts (higher memory/CPU), the blended $/1M rises ~12–18% vs pure 8k workload.
- Rough POC pro forma: at 513M tokens/month a blended $/1M of $18 => monthly cost ~ $9.234k. At $14/1M => ~$7.182k.

Context-length sensitivity (rule-of-thumb multipliers vs 8k baseline):
- 8k context: baseline x1.0
- 32k context: ~x1.4–1.7 (kernel switching, KV cache pressure)
- 128k context: ~x2.5–3.2 (heavy memory and IO; likely reserved/dedicated infra)

So if your 1% >8k and 0.1% >32k, the effective blended multiplier ≈ 1.02–1.05 over baseline assuming smart routing to cheaper variants for small prompts. That maps to the ~12–18% blended increase noted above (spread due to batching assumptions).

Targeting procurement ask (your $20k–$45k/month): based on the numbers you shared, we can model three purchase options:
A) Hosted pay-as-you-go POC (no commitment): higher $/1M but no upfront commit; good for short exploratory testing.
B) 3-month reserved POC (modest commit): ~10–18% discount vs pay-as-you-go for committed volume; recommended if you want stable unit price.
C) Dedicated pool (for high percent of >8k/32k): upfront committed capacity; best latency and predictable pricing for heavy long-context usage.

I uploaded the scenario sheet and a quick cost simulation. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cFinovate-Proposals (redwood_cost_sim.xlsx).

Would you like me to pick nominal numbers and put together a formal quick quote (with options A/B/C) for procurement? If yes, tell me which option you prefer to see first — I suggest B (3-month reserved) as a middle ground.

— Ben

Attachments: redwood_cost_sim.xlsx
